evidence.excerpt: The contribution of this work is architectural rather than methodological at the model level: we use only standard, publicly available frontier LLMs, and demonstrate that when combined across providers, embedded in a hierarchical multi‐agent architecture, and augmented by the cognitive operators and dynamic memory systems described above ‐ these techniques are jointly sufficient to conduct empirical science autonomously from hypothesis generation through to manuscript preparation.
evidence.explanation: The contribution is explicitly stated in the Discussion section as architectural rather than methodological at the model level.
evidence.paraphrase: The paper clearly states its contribution as an architectural demonstration of end-to-end autonomous scientific discovery with human participants.

evidence.excerpt: The system leverages a hierarchical multi‐agent architecture [ 59 ] to autonomously produce scientific research through the coordinated and collaborative efforts of a task force of specialized AI agents (Figure  1 ).
evidence.explanation: The Methods section describes a hierarchical multi-agent architecture with orchestrators and specialists, and four cognitive operators (abstraction, metacognition, decomposition, autonomy).
evidence.paraphrase: The system architecture is described with specific components and cognitive operators.

evidence.excerpt: There are (currently) no objective tests with which to evaluate the quality of scientific manuscripts; thus, here we employed structured expert review (mirroring established peer review processes) to assess the AI‐generated manuscripts.
evidence.explanation: The Results section describes structured expert review mirroring established peer review processes.
evidence.paraphrase: Human expert evaluation was conducted to assess the AI-generated manuscripts.

evidence.excerpt: Theoretical models were occasionally misrepresented, including inappropriate extension of a VWM framework [ 120 ] to unrelated visuospatial tasks in Study 3, and Study 2's false claim about working memory resource al
evidence.explanation: The negative aspects section of the expert evaluation reveals issues that undermine the claim of rigor comparable to experienced researchers.
evidence.paraphrase: The expert evaluation identified substantive problems in the AI-generated manuscripts, including theoretical misrepresentations and false claims.

evidence.excerpt: The system executed full studies (from initial conception to manuscript) in ∼17 h runtime on average per study, excluding data collection. Comparatively, typical human‐led workflows can require weeks to months of human expert time depending on experimental complexity.
evidence.explanation: Runtime, token usage, cost, and code generation metrics are reported in Table 1 and the Results section.
evidence.paraphrase: The paper reports quantitative system performance metrics that support the feasibility claim.
